title: A Extraction for the Deadline
premise: Jonah Okonkwo, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent years laundering her own identity into something unremarkable, is pulled back in when a dead colleague's voiceprint unlocks a server in Lagos containing proof of a coordinated attack disguised as an industrial accident. The trail runs through the very clean-money networks she audits, implicating the mentor who once gave her a place to belong and the found family she built inside the agency. As a border checkpoint shift change becomes the attack's window, Jonah must choose between exposing everyone she loves or letting power's machinery grind forward. In the end she burns her own cover to stop the attack, loses the family that made invisibility bearable, and walks away carrying the truth no one will officially believe.
about_author: Orsen Hartwell is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction full-time. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to make them look away.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet her mid-audit, flagging clean money with practiced boredom while her packed bag sits by the door and her rehearsed cover story hums underneath everything. A routine ping from an old colleague's account unsettles her calm. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on leaving.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The dead colleague's voicemail greeting unlocks a Lagos server using her voice as the key. Inside: schematics, payment ledgers, and a countdown tied to a border checkpoint rotation. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past reaching across continents to claim her.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She traces the ledger entries into accounts she herself has cleared over three years, realizing her own sign-offs are woven into the plot's funding. Emotional beat: horror at complicity; the auditor audited.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Table
chapters.summary: Alternate POV: Deputy Director Adaeze Cole, Jonah's mentor, hosting a quiet dinner where power is passed like wine. She approves a 'logistics adjustment' without reading it. Emotional beat: corruption as comfort, evil as paperwork.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Flashback-woven present: how the agency became her first real family after years of running—shared meals, inside jokes, Adaeze's protection. Now every warmth reads as surveillance. Emotional beat: grief for a family that may be a cage.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Math
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She decodes the timing: the attack is scheduled for the ninety-minute window when the checkpoint shifts change and oversight goes dark. She calculates she has eleven days. Emotional beat: cold clarity sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Mail
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Her queries trip a tripwire; a car idles outside her building; her go-bag feels suddenly insufficient. She moves to a safehouse run by Tunde, an ex-analyst she trusts. Emotional beat: paranoia becoming intimacy—trust as risk.

chapters.title: Tunde's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Tunde's POV. He cooks for Jonah, tells his own story of being burned by the institution, and agrees to help. Their alliance forms over jollof rice and redacted files. Emotional beat: found family forming in real time, fragile and chosen.

chapters.title: The Shell Garden
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Peeling the corporate shells, she finds a front company whose board includes two agency names she knows—and one she loves. Emotional beat: dread tightening; loyalty and evidence pulling opposite directions.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Warning
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. She summons Jonah, gently, terribly, offering promotion and warning her off 'old ghosts.' It's both threat and genuine care. Emotional beat: seduction of power; the reader sees Adaeze believes she's protecting Jonah.

chapters.title: Eleven Days to Nine
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Clock chapters begin. She and Tunde map the target—a refinery adjacent to the checkpoint—and realize the 'accident' would kill hundreds and bury the ledger trail forever. Emotional beat: stakes made human via named potential victims.

chapters.title: The Insider
chapters.summary: Tunde's POV. They identify the inside man: Marcus, Jonah's closest friend at the agency, coerced through debt and blackmail rather than greed. Emotional beat: heartbreak—corruption's victims include its instruments.

chapters.title: Confrontation in Parking Level Two
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She corners Marcus; he breaks, gives her the operational details but refuses to testify, terrified for his daughter. Emotional beat: compassion versus necessity; no clean hands anywhere.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. The conspiracy detects the leak. Orders go out to erase Jonah—quietly, deniably. Adaeze hesitates one beat too long, revealing her conflict. Emotional beat: the mentor's mask cracking.

chapters.title: Run
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. An ambush at the safehouse; Tunde is wounded covering her escape. She finally grabs the go-bag—but this time she's running toward something, not away. Emotional beat: transformation; flight becomes charge.

chapters.title: What Tunde Knew
chapters.summary: Tunde's POV, hospital bed. Before losing consciousness he passes Jonah the last key: proof Adaeze signed the funding release under duress years ago—she was compromised before she was corrupt. Emotional beat: complicating the villain into a tragedy.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Adaeze calls: stand down and be restored, protected, family again—or burn alone. Jonah hears the love in it and refuses anyway. Emotional beat: choosing truth over belonging; the theme crystallized.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Split POV, real time. Ninety minutes to the checkpoint rotation. Jonah and Marcus race to trigger a manual override while conspirators move to accelerate the schedule. Emotional beat: breathless momentum, every paragraph a countdown.

chapters.title: The Accident That Didn't Happen
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Climax. She kills the ignition sequence seconds before detonation, exposes the operation on an open channel so it can't be quietly buried, and faces down the fixer sent to erase her. Emotional beat: triumph laced with cost—she wins by making herself permanently visible.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Arrests, spin, official reports that soften everything. Adaeze resigns before they can fire her, leaving Jonah a letter that is half apology, half warning. Emotional beat: bitter vindication; institutions absorb even their exposures.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She unpacks the go-bag item by item, keeping only a photograph of Tunde, Marcus, and herself from better years. Tunde recovers; Marcus takes a plea deal; the family survives, changed. Emotional beat: mourning and gratitude braided together.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Invisible
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue. Months later, she testifies under her real name, no longer hiding, working cases that matter with people who know all of her. The final image: the door left unlocked. Emotional beat: peace earned—belonging chosen over safety.
